title: openrig studio — app manifest, app.json (contract v0.1)
description: Declares an APP: a surface plus the backend it calls, the directories it needs, and the binaries it requires. Stability: fields marked x-stability 'stable' change only additively while the contract is 0.x; 'provisional' fields may change with a minor bump. Field semantics and the reconciliation rules are in app-manifest.md. A fact belongs to the thing that knows it — how to RUN a provider and which verbs it ANSWERS live in the provider's own provider.json, never here.

manifest_version.description: Manifest format version. Bumped only for a breaking change to this shape.

id.description: Unique app id. Becomes the surface row id, so it is also a deep-link target.

name.description: Rail label. Short, uppercase by convention.

summary.description: One line describing what the app is for. Shown in listings.

category.description: Grouping hint (create | build | grow | system by convention).

maker.description: Attribution only. Never used to resolve or install anything.

surface.description: The page. Exactly one of path or url — path means the shell serves this file, url means something else already does.

entry.description: Where the file lives in YOUR repo. The composer copies it into the overlay. Required with path; meaningless with url.

path.description: Where it is served on the rail. Different from entry, and conflating the two is the common slip.

url.description: Absolute http(s) URL for an app that serves itself.

glyph.description: One character. The rail is dense; an emoji looks wrong beside the others.

hint.description: One-line tooltip on the rail tab.

provider.description: A REFERENCE to the backend this app is a client of. Not a run spec — how to start it lives in that provider's provider.json. Singular on purpose: dependencies on OTHER backends are declared in calls.

required.description: true when the app is useless without it. Installing a surface whose provider is absent yields an HTML file that 502s.

roots.description: The KINDS of directory this app needs — never paths. The box binds each kind to a real location in studio.json. Kind names are an OPEN vocabulary.

required.description: true when the app cannot work without this root bound.

calls.description: The /api/ verbs this app calls, keyed by verb. Deliberately provider-agnostic: the box resolves which installed provider answers each one, so this must not name a package. This is how an app depends on a verb a DIFFERENT provider serves.

required.description: true when the app does not work without this verb. Declared rather than derived because only the author knows whether an unserved verb is a missing nicety or a dead product. A required unmatched call may start the provider that serves it; an optional one starts nothing.

vendor.description: Bare directory names under the app's vendor/ directory, shipped with the app so the box never calls a CDN. Prose in this field reads fine to a human and installs nothing.

requires.description: What the app needs from the host, whoever satisfies it. A provider may declare that it SHIPS a binary; that does not make the need untrue, so both stay legible.

binaries.description: Binaries the app needs on PATH or supplied by its provider.

ffmpeg_filters.description: Filters without which the app cannot work. Absence is fatal to an install.

ffmpeg_filters_preferred.description: Filters that degrade a feature when absent. Must NOT block an install — losing a caption is not worth refusing a working studio.

verbs.description: LEGACY, superseded by calls. Was an app-authored list that the box also consumed as the provider routing table — two facts in one field, so an app's focus verb worked only while some other app happened to declare it. Honoured while the provider ships no provider.json, with a warning. Use calls.
